import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_92/test_0.csv"
        # If there were more sources, they would be added here
    ]

    # List to hold dataframes from all sources
    dfs = []

    # Load each source file, ensure schema matches target schema, and append to list
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

        # Normalize column names to lowercase to avoid case issues
        df.columns = [col.lower() for col in df.columns]

        # Rename columns if needed to match target schema exactly
        # Target schema: ['user_id', 'email', 'geo'] all lowercase
        # Source schema is already ['user_id', 'email', 'geo'] but user_id might have different casing in values

        # Convert user_id to lowercase to match target style (target examples show lowercase user_id)
        df['user_id'] = df['user_id'].str.lower()

        # Strip whitespace from email and geo columns just in case
        df['email'] = df['email'].str.strip()
        df['geo'] = df['geo'].str.strip()

        # Append to list
        dfs.append(df[['user_id', 'email', 'geo']])

    # Concatenate all source dataframes vertically (union)
    target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Optional: Remove duplicates if any (not specified but often useful)
    target_df = target_df.drop_duplicates()

    # Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file
    target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_92/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
